fullPassage:
People often omit the period at the end of sentences in single-sentence text messages, which has influenced the way we perceive periods. In an experiment, participants reading text messages found single sentences with a period less sincere than those without one. This could be due to something called "situational code-switching," which simply means that we change how we talk depending on the social setting. For example, the language that students use in the classroom is different from the language they use on the playground. If they talked to their friends the same way they talked to their teachers, it would probably sound strange. Similarly, a person using periods in text messages can cause feelings of awkwardness, just like someone using formal language in a casual setting.

In the 1800s, the people of Ireland used potatoes as their basic food source. Unfortunately, everyone was growing the same type of potato, which meant the crops all had the same genes. The farmers did not realize the danger in this. In the 1840s, a new potato disease struck. The genetically identical potatoes all lacked the ability to fight the disease, so they all rotted. Because people were dependent mainly on potatoes for their food, Ireland suffered a famine in which one in eight people died during the following years. If people had grown many types of potatoes, they could have identified resistant ones and grown more of them, making the famine less serious. Despite knowing this, many countries today take the same risk with their crops.

In 1985, my husband and I moved to his hometown, located in China's Ordas Desert. When I first saw our new home, I burst into tears. There was nothing but sand for miles around. "I wish I could see some plants," I thought. Then one day I saw a small tree growing beside a nearby well. I realized that if this tree could survive, others might be able to, too. I started to plant more trees. At first, many of them ended up buried in sandstorms, but my husband and I eventually managed to get most of the trees to survive. We have now planted more than 600,000 trees in the desert. We have turned one of the most desolate places in China into something beautiful.

Socotra Island, a small island owned by Yemen and located in the Arabian Sea, looks as if it were part of another planet. In fact, it separated from the mainland of Africa six or seven million years ago, causing unique forms of life to develop on it. It is home to about 800 species of rare plants and animals, many of which are found nowhere else on earth. Because the island experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts, many of its plants have evolved unusual appearances. One striking example is the dragon's blood tree. Its branches make it look like a giant umbrella. It gets its name from a thick, red substance that comes out when its bark is cut. When this happens, it appears as if the tree were bleeding.

Everyone on Earth may soon lose one second of time. For the first time ever, scientists are considering subtracting a single second. This is called a "negative leap second," and it may be necessary in 2029 because Earth is rotating slightly faster than before. Surprisingly, without global warming, this time change would likely have been necessary sooner. The reason Earth is spinning faster is the unpredictable behavior of its hot liquid core. This behavior has been causing an increase in speed for approximately 50 years, but the melting of polar ice has been counteracting this effect. Melting ice raises sea levels and shifts the planet's mass away from the poles and toward the equator. This slows the Earth's rotation in the same way that figure skaters spin more slowly when extending their arms outward. Without the melting of polar ice, it is likely that we would need to lose a second in 2026 rather than 2029. "We are headed toward a negative leap second," said one expert. "It's a matter of when."

The origins of flags probably began with warriors decorating their spears with colored ribbons as a way of distinguishing one army from another. This practice was adopted by early explorers, who started using flags to show who newly discovered lands belonged to. During the modern era, flags became a symbol of individual nations, and it has become accepted that every country must have its own flag. Most of these national flags are roughly the same size and shape. They commonly feature bold colors and simple patterns, as flags with intricate patterns would appear distorted when blowing in the wind.

Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a significant transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to obtain hydrogen. This allowed them to assimilate carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then released oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.

Being alone makes us more creative. Many great artists and thinkers throughout history have lived by themselves. When we are alone, we have fewer distractions. This allows our thoughts to run free without interruption or judgment. Creative people have entire worlds inside their heads, and being alone gives them the opportunity to bring ideas from this inner world into the real world. Steve Wozniak, for example, invented the Apple computer sitting alone at a desk. He says his creativity came from being introverted as a child. Had it not been for his shyness, he might not have become a computer expert. However, this does not mean we should stop working together with others. Had it not been for Wozniak's collaboration with Steve Jobs, he could not have started his own business. Therefore, we should seek out solitude, but only when we need it.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: read → reading (한 문장에 본동사 found가 이미 있으므로 participants를 꾸미는 분사 reading)

② called: 'something called ~' '~라고 불리는' 과거분사 — 적절
③ that: 'the language that students use' 관계대명사 — 적절
④ cause: 'can cause' 조동사 뒤 동사원형 — 적절
det.tip: 한 문장에 본동사(found)가 이미 있으면 나머지는 분사로. participants reading(참가자들이 읽던)

det.korean: which → in which (뒤 문장이 완전하고 '기근 속에서' 죽었다는 뜻이므로 전치사+관계대명사 in which)

② identical: 'The genetically identical potatoes'에서 명사 potatoes를 앞에서 꾸미는 형용사 — 적절

④ take: 'many countries today take the same risk' 현재의 일반적 사실을 나타내는 현재동사 — 적절
det.tip: 뒤 문장이 완전 + '~속에서'라는 뜻 → 전치사+관계대명사 in which

det.korean: ① combining→distinguishing (부적절) ② adopted=채택된 ③ accepted=받아들여진 ④ simple=단순한

④ simple: 국기는 '단순한' 무늬를 특징으로 함 — 적절해요.
det.tip: 한 군대를 다른 군대와 distinguishing(구별). combining(결합)은 정반대
